author: Rodrigo Tobar <rtobar@icrar.org>
message:
Add new all_subhalos_view type

The all_subhalos_view type is a container-like class (it offers both
begin() and end() methods) that can be used to iterate over the subhalos
of a halo, as well as to count how many subhalos there are contained in
a halo. Iteration happens by visiting the central subhalo first, if any,
and then the satellites. The implementation of this visitation pattern
is implemented in the inner iterator class.

This commit introduces the new type, but doesn't update the rest of the
code to use it yet.

Signed-off-by: Rodrigo Tobar <rtobar@icrar.org>

author: Rodrigo Tobar <rtobar@icrar.org>
message:
Reimplement all_subhalos using all_subhalos_view

The change was almost transparent, with some exceptions which I describe
below.

First, the code defining the central subhalo for each Halo was relying
on the first element of all_subhalos() being the most massive, which
isn't the case anymore. We do this explicitly now for this specific
case. This same code was also relying on all_subhalos() returning new
SubhaloPtr objects, so it could safely remove the satellite subhalo from
the underlying Halo::satellite_subhalos vector and still keep using it.
This isn't the case now either: the all_subhalos_view object returns
direct references to the underlying vector, so once a satellite is
removed from the vector the SubhaloPtr isn't valid anymore (most of the
times, unless someone else is pointing to it). The solution is obviously
to make a copy on this case.

The other exception was the code performing the linking between
snapshots, which removes subhalos *while iterating over them*. This
worked before because we always returned a new vector, and therefore
removing subhalos from the Halo had no effect on the iteration over the
vector. We explicitly create a new vector for this iteration now, which
then makes the code happy.

A set of unit tests also demonstrates the new functionality is working
as intended in all the possible use cases.

Signed-off-by: Rodrigo Tobar <rtobar@icrar.org>

author: Claudia Lagos <claudia.lagos@icrar.org>
message:
Limiting halo gas to universal baryon fraction

Testing limiting the reincorporated mass and pritine accretion to keep
the halo baryon fraction equal or below the universal baryon fraction.
This is checked as total baryon (including ejected and lost baryons), as
well as baryons inside halos (excluding ejected and lost baryons).

Another important change is the way we ensure mass growth in the trees.
The way it was done before didn't consider the many progenitors a halo
can have. I corrected that and now it's consistent.

author: Claudia Lagos <claudia.lagos@icrar.org>
message:
Changes to environment and AGN quenching

- In environment we are assuming that the ejected gas reservoir of
galaxies is lost once the halo becomes a subhalo (when galaxies become
satellites). This us supported by the work of Ruby Wright in EAGLE.

- In gas_cooling: Bravo19 model should also adopt the assumption of Croton16
that rheat can only increase.
